column4: Difficult to distinguish the explosion noted to have occurred prior to this event by Waythomas and others (2013) and the lahar signal, impossible to distinguish on the closest stations because they are all clipped, so we picked start times using station DFR (~12 km from source area, closer to runout area), where a secondary pulse is clearer in the spectrogram (change in frequency content).

Waythomas and others (2013) states that Lahar 6 was one of the largest lahars of the eruption and also shows that the amplitude was about 5x higher than for lahar 5. Lahar 5 and 6 are lumped together in the volume calculation, with a combined estimate of 1 to 6 x 10^7 m3. We assumed that range and assumed that 3/4 of each total is Lahar 6, 1/4 is Lahar 5. We use total volume of 3.5e7 m3 for best estimate.
Volume and geometry estimates from information in Waythomas and others (2013)
Start time and duration, therefore end times, guided by Waythomas and others (2013), particularly Figure 3.
It is not clear if the long period signals visible during some of the Redoubt lahars were due to the lahar or other volcanic processes such as explosions or tremor.
